_about: The covenant words side by side (plan 7.6b): wordings of covenant that more than one book shares, from Noah and Abraham to Sinai, David, the prophets and the Last Supper, each set out where it is used, with what is alike and what differs. Every quotation machine-checked against the Berean; rows chosen and drafted by Claude Opus from the passages the theme map cites, the Berean editors' quotation notes and a search of the whole Berean; widened by the completeness search; every Alike and Different line read by the nine-reader panel (Sonnet). Takes no interpretive stance. A cell [verse, words, "aside"] is off the subject and shown, with an asterisk, for its shared words.
columns_note: The Law & history: Genesis to Esther. Psalms & wisdom: Job to the Song of Solomon. The Prophets: Isaiah to Malachi.

rows.title: I will establish My covenant

The Law & history: I will establish My covenant with you
I establish My covenant with you
the covenant that I have established between Me and every creature on the earth
I will establish My covenant between Me and you
I will establish My covenant as an everlasting covenant
I will establish My covenant with him
I will establish My covenant with Isaac
I also established My covenant with them
I will establish My covenant with you
The Prophets: If I have not established My covenant with the day and the night
So I will establish My covenant with you
The letters: the covenant previously established by God

rows.alike: In each the covenant is God's to establish: "I will establish My covenant with you" is said in Genesis 6:18, Leviticus 26:9 and Ezekiel 16:62, and "I will establish My covenant" recurs through Genesis 17.
rows.different: The ones it is established with differ: "with you" (Genesis 6:18), "with Isaac" (Genesis 17:21), "with them" (Exodus 6:4), "with the day and the night" (Jeremiah 33:25). Galatians 3:17 alone speaks of it in the third person, "the covenant previously established by God", and says "The law that came 430 years later does not revoke" it.

rows.title: An everlasting covenant

The Law & history: the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature
as an everlasting covenant between Me and you and your descendants after you
My covenant in your flesh will be an everlasting covenant
as an everlasting covenant for his descendants after him
He has established with me an everlasting covenant
to Israel as an everlasting covenant
Psalms & wisdom: to Israel as an everlasting covenant
The Prophets: I will make with you an everlasting covenant-My loving devotion promised to David
make an everlasting covenant with them
I will make an everlasting covenant with them
join themselves to the LORD in an everlasting covenant that will never be forgotten
I will establish an everlasting covenant with you

rows.alike: All use the words "everlasting covenant": in Genesis 9 and 17, in 2 Samuel 23:5, in 1 Chronicles 16:17 and Psalm 105:10 (word for word alike), and in Isaiah, Jeremiah and Ezekiel.
rows.different: Genesis 9:16 sets it "between God and every living creature"; Genesis 17:7 sets it with "your descendants after you"; 2 Samuel 23:5 says "He has established with me". Isaiah 55:3, 61:8 and Jeremiah 32:40 speak of making it: "I will make with you an everlasting covenant", "make an everlasting covenant with them", "I will make an everlasting covenant with them"; Isaiah 24:5 says the earth's people have "broken the everlasting covenant". Isaiah 55:3 adds "My loving devotion promised to David"; Jeremiah 50:5 adds "that will never be forgotten".

rows.title: A sign between Me and you

The Law & history: This is the sign of the covenant I am making between Me and you
I have set My rainbow in the clouds, and it will be a sign of the covenant between Me and the earth
This is the sign of the covenant
this will be a sign of the covenant between Me and you
Surely you must keep My Sabbaths, for this will be a sign between Me and you for the generations to come
It is a sign between Me and the Israelites forever
The Prophets: I also gave them My Sabbaths as a sign between us
Keep My Sabbaths holy, that they may be a sign between us

rows.alike: Each names something as "a sign" set "between Me and you" or "between us": "My rainbow in the clouds" (Genesis 9:13), circumcision (Genesis 17:11), and "My Sabbaths" (Exodus 31:13; Ezekiel 20:12, 20).
rows.different: In these verses, "a sign of the covenant" is said only in Genesis 9 and 17. Exodus 31:13 and Ezekiel 20:12 give the sign a purpose in nearly the same words, "so that you may know that I am the LORD who sanctifies you" and "so that they would know that I am the LORD who sanctifies them". Genesis 9:13 sets the sign "between Me and the earth"; Exodus 31:17 "between Me and the Israelites forever".

rows.title: The covenant of circumcision

The Law & history: Every male among you must be circumcised
You are to circumcise the flesh of your foreskin
every male must be circumcised when he is eight days old
they must be circumcised. My covenant in your flesh
if any male is not circumcised, he will be cut off from his people
When his son Isaac was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him, as God had commanded him
Gospels & Acts: God gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision, and Abraham became the father of Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day
The letters: he received the sign of circumcision

rows.alike: Genesis 17 gives circumcision to Abraham as "My covenant in your flesh", "when he is eight days old"; Acts 7:8 calls it "the covenant of circumcision" and repeats that Abraham "circumcised him on the eighth day".
rows.different: Genesis 17:11 calls it "a sign of the covenant"; Romans 4:11 calls it "the sign of circumcision" and adds "as a seal of the righteousness that he had by faith while he was still uncircumcised". Genesis 17:14 alone states the penalty: "he will be cut off from his people".

rows.title: Circumcise your hearts

The Law & history: if their uncircumcised hearts will be humbled
Circumcise your hearts, therefore, and stiffen your necks no more
The LORD your God will circumcise your hearts and the hearts of your descendants
The Prophets: Circumcise yourselves to the LORD, and remove the foreskins of your hearts
all who are circumcised only in the flesh
the whole house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart
foreigners uncircumcised in both heart and flesh
No foreigner uncircumcised in heart and flesh may enter My sanctuary
Gospels & Acts: You stiff-necked people with uncircumcised hearts and ears!
The letters: nor is circumcision only outward and physical
circumcision is a matter of the heart

rows.alike: Each speaks of circumcision of the heart: "Circumcise your hearts" (Deuteronomy 10:16), "remove the foreskins of your hearts" (Jeremiah 4:4), "uncircumcised in heart" (Jeremiah 9:26; Ezekiel 44:9), "uncircumcised hearts" (Leviticus 26:41; Acts 7:51), "circumcision is a matter of the heart" (Romans 2:29).
rows.different: Deuteronomy 10:16 and Jeremiah 4:4 command it of the hearers; Deuteronomy 30:6 says "The LORD your God will circumcise your hearts". Ezekiel 44 pairs "heart and flesh"; Jeremiah 9:25 speaks of those "circumcised only in the flesh"; Acts 7:51 says "hearts and ears" and has "stiff-necked people", where Deuteronomy 10:16 has "stiffen your necks no more". Romans 2:29 adds "by the Spirit, not by the written code".

rows.title: He remembers His covenant

The Law & history: I will remember My covenant between Me and you and every living creature
I will see it and remember the everlasting covenant

I will remember the covenant with their fathers

Psalms & wisdom: He remembers His covenant forever, the word He ordained for a thousand generations
He remembered His covenant with them
The Prophets: I will remember the covenant I made with you

rows.alike: Each speaks of remembering the covenant: "I will remember My covenant" (Genesis 9:15; Leviticus 26:42), "He remembered His covenant" (Exodus 2:24; Psalm 106:45), "He remembers His covenant forever" (Psalm 105:8; 111:5), "Remember Your covenant with us" (Jeremiah 14:21), "to remember His holy covenant" (Luke 1:72).
rows.different: 1 Chronicles 16:15 has the call "Remember His covenant forever" where Psalm 105:8 has "He remembers His covenant forever", the rest of the line alike. In Genesis 9:16 the rainbow is the prompt: "I will see it and remember". Jeremiah 14:21 is the people's plea, "Remember Your covenant with us"; Exodus 2:24 and 6:5 follow hearing the "groaning" of the Israelites.

rows.title: Keep My covenant

The Law & history: he kept Your word and maintained Your covenant
have not kept My covenant and My statutes
Psalms & wisdom: to those who keep His covenant and His decrees
They failed to keep God's covenant and refused to live by His law
to those who keep His covenant and remember to obey His precepts
If your sons keep My covenant
The Prophets: who keep My Sabbaths, who choose what pleases Me and hold fast to My covenant
who keep the Sabbath without profaning it and who hold fast to My covenant
this covenant I had commanded them to follow but they did not keep
surviving only by keeping his covenant

rows.alike: Each speaks of people who "keep" the covenant or fail to: "You must keep My covenant" (Genesis 17:9), "those who keep His covenant" (Psalm 25:10; 103:18), "have not kept My covenant" (1 Kings 11:11), "They failed to keep God's covenant" (Psalm 78:10).
rows.different: The covenant is paired with other things kept: "and My statutes" (1 Kings 11:11), "and His decrees" (Psalm 25:10), "His law" (Psalm 78:10), "My Sabbaths" (Isaiah 56:4). Psalm 132:12 reads "If your sons keep My covenant"; Isaiah 56 says it of "the eunuchs" and "the foreigners" and uses "hold fast to My covenant". Ezekiel 17:14, shown only for the shared words, has the kingdom "surviving only by keeping his covenant".

rows.title: Who keeps His covenant of loving devotion

The Law & history: showing loving devotion to a thousand generations of those who love Me and keep My commandments
showing loving devotion to a thousand generations of those who love Me and keep My commandments
the faithful God who keeps His covenant of loving devotion for a thousand generations of those who love Him and keep His commandments
the LORD your God will keep His covenant and the loving devotion that He swore to your fathers
keeping Your covenant of loving devotion with Your servants who walk before You with all their hearts
keeping Your covenant of loving devotion with Your servants who walk before You with all their hearts
the great and awesome God who keeps His covenant of loving devotion with those who love Him and keep His commandments
the great and mighty and awesome God who keeps His gracious covenant
The Prophets: the great and awesome God, who keeps His covenant of loving devotion to those who love Him and keep His commandments

rows.alike: Deuteronomy 7:9, Nehemiah 1:5 and Daniel 9:4 share "keeps His covenant of loving devotion" and "those who love Him and keep His commandments"; Exodus 20:6 and Deuteronomy 5:10 have "loving devotion to a thousand generations of those who love Me and keep My commandments".
rows.different: Exodus 20:6 and Deuteronomy 5:10 do not say "covenant". Nehemiah 1:5 and Daniel 9:4 are addressed to God and both say "the great and awesome God"; 1 Kings 8:23 and 2 Chronicles 6:14 both say "keeping Your covenant of loving devotion with Your servants who walk before You with all their hearts"; Nehemiah 9:32 says "His gracious covenant". Deuteronomy 7:12 reads "If you listen to these ordinances and keep them carefully, then the LORD your God will keep His covenant".

rows.title: They broke My covenant

The Law & history: They will forsake Me and break the covenant I have made with them
they will reject Me and break My covenant
The Prophets: have broken the covenant I made with their fathers
Can he break a covenant and yet escape?
He despised the oath by breaking the covenant

rows.alike: Each says the covenant is broken by people: "he has broken My covenant" (Genesis 17:14), "break My covenant" (Leviticus 26:15; Deuteronomy 31:20), "you broke My covenant" (Ezekiel 44:7), "have broken the covenant I made with their fathers" (Jeremiah 11:10).
rows.different: In Deuteronomy 31:16 and 31:20 the LORD says it ahead of time ("They will forsake Me and break the covenant"); in Jeremiah 11:10 and Ezekiel 44:7 it is said as done. Isaiah 24:5 says it of "The earth" and "its people". In Ezekiel 17 the covenant broken is first "whose covenant he broke", a king's, then "My covenant that he broke". Amos 1:9 says it of Tyre and "a covenant of brotherhood".

rows.title: I will never break My covenant

The Law & history: I will not reject or despise them so as to destroy them and break My covenant with them
I will never break My covenant with you
reject Me and break My covenant
Psalms & wisdom: I will not violate My covenant or alter the utterance of My lips
The Prophets: My covenant of peace will not be broken
If you can break My covenant with the day and My covenant with the night
then My covenant may also be broken with David My servant

rows.alike: Several have the LORD say His covenant will not be broken: "I will never break My covenant with you" (Judges 2:1), "I will not ... break My covenant with them" (Leviticus 26:44), "I will not violate My covenant" (Psalm 89:34), "My covenant of peace will not be broken" (Isaiah 54:10).
rows.different: Leviticus 26:44 says it of a time "when they are in the land of their enemies"; Isaiah 54:10 sets it against "the mountains may be removed and the hills may be shaken". Jeremiah 33:20-21 makes it a comparison: "If you can break My covenant with the day and My covenant with the night" ... "then My covenant may also be broken with David My servant". Jeremiah 14:21 is the people asking, "do not break it". Leviticus 26:15 and Deuteronomy 31:20 use "break My covenant" of the people who do it.

rows.title: Transgressed the covenant

The Law & history: they have transgressed My covenant that I commanded them

Psalms & wisdom: they were unfaithful to His covenant
The Prophets: those who have transgressed My covenant
But they, like Adam, have transgressed the covenant; there they were unfaithful to Me
the people have transgressed My covenant and rebelled against My law
You have violated the covenant of Levi

rows.alike: Each speaks of the covenant being transgressed, violated or dealt with unfaithfully: "they have transgressed My covenant" (Joshua 7:11; Hosea 8:1 "the people have transgressed My covenant"), "violated His covenant" (2 Kings 18:12), "they were unfaithful to His covenant" (Psalm 78:37).
rows.different: Joshua 7:11 and 23:16 add that it was "commanded"; 2 Kings 18:12 adds "all that Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded"; Hosea 8:1 adds "and rebelled against My law"; Hosea 6:7 and Psalm 78:37 say "unfaithful". Malachi 2:8 names "the covenant of Levi"; Psalm 55:20 says it of a "companion" who "violates his covenant".

rows.title: Forsaken, forgotten the covenant

Psalms & wisdom: we have not forgotten You or betrayed Your covenant

The Prophets: Because they have forsaken the covenant of the LORD their God
an everlasting covenant that will never be forgotten
those who forsake the holy covenant

rows.alike: Each speaks of the covenant abandoned, forsaken or forgotten: "do not forget the covenant" (Deuteronomy 4:23; 2 Kings 17:38), "they abandoned the covenant of the LORD" (Deuteronomy 29:25), "have forsaken Your covenant" (1 Kings 19:10, 14), "they have forsaken the covenant of the LORD their God" (Jeremiah 22:9).
rows.different: Deuteronomy 29:25 has the people "answer" and Jeremiah 22:9 has people "reply": "It is because they abandoned" and "Because they have forsaken". 1 Kings 19:10 and 19:14 give the same words twice. Deuteronomy 4:31 turns it to God, who will not "forget the covenant with your fathers"; Psalm 44:17 says "though we have not forgotten You or betrayed Your covenant"; Proverbs 2:17 says it of one who "forgets the covenant of her God".

rows.title: The blood of the covenant

The Law & history: This is the blood of the covenant that the LORD has made with you in accordance with all these words
The Prophets: because of the blood of My covenant, I will release your prisoners from the waterless pit

rows.alike: Exodus 24:8 and Hebrews 9:20 share "This is the blood of the covenant"; Matthew 26:28 and Mark 14:24 have "This is My blood of the covenant"; Zechariah 9:11 has "the blood of My covenant".
rows.different: In Exodus 24:8 Moses says it over blood "splattered" on the people, the covenant "that the LORD has made with you"; Hebrews 9:20 has "which God has commanded you to keep". In Matthew and Mark it is "My blood", "poured out for many", and Matthew adds "for the forgiveness of sins". Hebrews 13:20 says "the eternal covenant"; Zechariah 9:11 joins it to "I will release your prisoners".

rows.alike: All use the words "the ark of the covenant", in Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua, Judges, Samuel, Kings and Chronicles; Jeremiah 3:16 and Hebrews 9:4 use the same words, and Revelation 11:19 has "the ark of His covenant".
rows.different: The name is lengthened in different places: "the ark of the covenant of the LORD", "the ark of the covenant of God", "the ark of the covenant of the LORD of Hosts" (1 Samuel 4:4), "the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth" (Joshua 3:11). Jeremiah 3:16 says "they will no longer discuss the ark of the covenant of the LORD"; Hebrews 9:4 says "the gold-covered ark of the covenant"; in Revelation 11:19 "the ark of His covenant appeared in His temple".

rows.title: The tablets of the covenant

The Law & history: He wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant-the Ten Commandments

rows.alike: Deuteronomy 9 and Hebrews 9:4 both say "the tablets of the covenant"; Exodus 34:28 calls what is written on them "the words of the covenant-the Ten Commandments"; 1 Kings 8:9 and 2 Chronicles 5:10 tie the tablets in the ark to the place "where the LORD had made a covenant with the Israelites".
rows.different: 1 Kings 8:9 says "There was nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets" and 2 Chronicles 5:10 "There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets"; Hebrews 9:4 lists inside the ark "the gold jar of manna, Aaron's staff that had budded, and the stone tablets of the covenant".

rows.alike: Each speaks of the covenant as words to be heard and done: "the words of the covenant" (Deuteronomy 29:1; 2 Kings 23:3), "the words of this covenant" (Deuteronomy 29:9; Jeremiah 11:2, 3, 6), "the Book of the Covenant" read to the people (Exodus 24:7; 2 Kings 23:2), and "the curses of the covenant" (Deuteronomy 29:21; Jeremiah 11:8 "the curses of this covenant").
rows.different: In Exodus 24:7 the people answer "All that the LORD has spoken we will do"; in 2 Kings 23:3 "all the people entered into the covenant". 2 Kings 23:2 and 2 Chronicles 34:30 are alike except "the priests and the prophets" against "the priests and the Levites", and "small and great" against "great and small". Jeremiah 11:3 puts it as a curse: "Cursed is the man who does not obey the words of this covenant".

rows.alike: The same two halves recur: God will "be your God" and they will be "My people" (Jeremiah 7:23 and 30:22; Ezekiel 36:28), "My own people" (Exodus 6:7) or "His people" (Deuteronomy 29:13).
rows.different: The order turns: "I will be your God, and you will be My people" (Jeremiah 7:23) against "you will be My people, and I will be your God" (Jeremiah 11:4; Ezekiel 36:28). Jeremiah 7:23 and 11:4 begin "Obey Me"; Leviticus and Numbers tie "to be your God" to "who brought you out of the land of Egypt". Deuteronomy 26:17-18 makes it two proclamations, "you have proclaimed that the LORD is your God" and "the LORD has proclaimed that you are His people"; Zechariah 13:9 puts the halves in two mouths, "They are My people" and "The LORD is our God"; in 2 Kings 11:17 it is a covenant Jehoiada made "that they would be the LORD's people".

rows.different: Deuteronomy 7:6, 14:2 and Psalm 135:4 say "chosen"; Deuteronomy 7:6 and 14:2 add "out of all peoples on the face of the earth". Malachi 3:17 places it "on the day when I prepare" it and adds "I will spare them as a man spares his own son". Titus 2:14 says "He gave Himself for us to redeem us from all lawlessness" and adds "zealous for good deeds".

rows.different: Genesis 15:18 and Nehemiah 9:8 join the covenant to the land, "To your descendants I have given this land" and "to give the land of the Canaanites". Luke 1:73 has "the oath He swore to our father Abraham"; Acts 3:25 speaks of "the covenant God made with your fathers" and quotes what was said to Abraham.

rows.different: Deuteronomy 4:31 and 8:18 speak of a covenant God "swore"; Ezekiel 16:59 and 17:19 of an oath "despised". Ezekiel 17:13 and 17:16 use the pair of covenants between men, "putting him under oath" and "whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke"; so do Genesis 26:28, 2 Kings 11:4 and Hosea 10:4.
